chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who had a wet dream, then when he awoke he found a small amount of moisture. He said: It is nothing, unless he is ill, for then he becomes weakened, so ghusl is obligatory upon him.

So this does not contradict the earlier report that ghusl becomes obligatory from the greater fluid, because it is not impossible that this fluid is itself the greater fluid, except that it comes out from the sick person little by little due to his weakness and lack of movement. For that reason, he عليه السلام differentiated in the report between the sick person and the healthy person, and that further clarifies it.

key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required after major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْأَكْبَرِ: the major fluid, meaning semen that necessitates ghusl
key_terms.بَلَلًا: moisture or wetness found upon waking
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: being ill or sick, which affects the ruling here

ai.seo_question: Does a small amount of moisture after a wet dream require ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a person who wakes after a wet dream and finds only a small amount of moisture. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between a healthy person and an ill person, making ghusl obligatory for the ill due to the possibility that the seminal fluid exits gradually because of weakness.
